A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same survey of code reasoning for software engineering. All pages, figures, tables, and appendices were readable, and relocated or split material could be matched.

before.justification: V1 synthesizes published work. Section 5 identifies the benchmark tables as compilations of author-reported and cross-reported results; no original empirical study is reported.

after.justification: V2 remains a literature survey. Section 6 explicitly states that performance results come directly from original papers; the added charts visualize this compilation rather than report independently produced empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: Neither version proposes a new algorithm or model. V2 reorganizes the taxonomy and adds descriptions of prior methods, including VisualCoder, without introducing an implemented procedure of its own.

E1.justification: The compiled evaluations retain the same APPS, HumanEval, MBPP, LiveCodeBench, CodeContests, M3ToolEval, and SWE-Bench coverage. Additional discussion of benchmarks and future test scenarios does not establish new evaluations.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the corresponding benchmark tables is retained. The additional CYCLE-1B score concerns an existing comparison method; newly cited methods such as VisualCoder are not added to the performance comparisons.

E3.justification: Corresponding tables retain their benchmark subsets, metrics, and stated evaluation conditions. V2 reports no new controlled evaluation or revised protocol; the additional CYCLE score is a reporting addition.

E4.justification: No ablation, robustness experiment, or empirical error analysis is added. The new charts largely visualize comparisons already discussed in v1, while error-injection and recovery benchmarks remain future-work proposals.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance testing for the compiled comparisons. The discussion of variance remains conceptual rather than statistical reporting.

E6.justification: V2 Table 3 adds CYCLE-1B at 10.9% pass@1 on APPS, absent from v1 Table 3. The other matched numerical entries across the benchmark tables are unchanged, and the main comparative trends are retained.

T1.justification: Neither version supplies original formal results or proofs. The locality-based explanation attributed to Prystawski et al. and the appendix descriptions of pass@k and n@k are retained; their relocation and expanded conceptual discussion do not add theory.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain a dedicated survey, taxonomy, and benchmark synthesis. V2 explicitly narrows the stated scope to inference-time reasoning, excludes purely training-time techniques, and foregrounds gaps in evaluation beyond code generation.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands the research agenda to programming paradigms, software-quality and integration-test feedback, agent error recovery, and tool orchestration. Sections 6 and 8 add explicit cross-paper comparability limitations, and the inference-scaling discussion acknowledges only one comparison against self-refinement. Earlier mechanism hypotheses are largely retained.

D1.justification: V2 adds a GitHub pointer to categorized survey resources and benchmark details, including HumanEval's average 7.7 tests and MBPP's three tests per problem. It also removes details such as SWE-Fixer’s 110k training pairs and AceCoder’s 20-test generation procedure. These are documentation changes.

R1.justification: V2 adds VisualCoder, Mei et al.'s context-engineering survey, and work on overthinking, TRAIL, agent traceability, and GAIA. A new survey-comparison table sharpens positioning, while some peripheral background citations disappear. The central relationship to earlier code and reasoning surveys remains intact.

P1.justification: V2 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, and conclusion; moves methodology near the beginning; integrates agents into the techniques section; reorganizes tasks; and separates comparisons from an expanded research agenda. The title, author order, and terminology also change.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a single-column layout, adds an inference schematic and five comparison charts, redraws the taxonomy, merges component tables, and adds a survey-comparison table. Benchmark tables move to the appendix, with MBPP and HumanEval tables split. Some new chart labels obscure metric distinctions.

improvement.justification: V2 clarifies the techniques/tasks distinction, acknowledges uncontrolled cross-paper comparisons, and turns broad future-work suggestions into concrete research questions. These improve usability and calibration. Gains are tempered by shortened technical descriptions and Figure 4's misleading pass@1 label for CodeContests results that Table 4 identifies as pass@5.
